identificationModule.briefTitle: Comparisons of the Therapeutic Effects of Dienogest and Danazol on Endometriosis

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The aim of this study is to evaluate the efficacy between dienogest and danazol.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription:
Objective: Women with adenomyosis or endometripsis are often suffered from dysmenorrhea or menorrhagia. Dienogest and danazol are frequently used for the treatment of endometriosis. However, there was no literature mentioned about which medication is better for the treatment of endometriosis. Thus, the aim of this study is to evaluate the efficacy between dienogest and danazol.

Methods: All consecutive women, who have endometriosis, will be randomized to receive dienogest or danazol treatment, and will assess symptoms severity, receive CA125 examination, sonographic examination at baseline, 4 weeks and 16 weeks after treatment.

primaryOutcomes.measure: The change of severity in dysmenorrhea
primaryOutcomes.description: Between-group difference in the score of global response assessment of dysmenorrhea

secondaryOutcomes.measure: The change of severity in urinary symptoms
secondaryOutcomes.description: Between-group difference in the score of UDI-6

secondaryOutcomes.measure: The change of severity in quality of life related to urinary symptoms
secondaryOutcomes.description: Between-group difference in the score of IIQ-7

secondaryOutcomes.measure: The change of severity in menstrual amount
secondaryOutcomes.description: Between-group difference in the score of global response assessment of menstrual amount

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* \> 20 years old
* Have an endometriosis-related condition (including adenomyosis, adenomyoma, ovarian endometrioma, or pelvic endometriosis).

Exclusion Criteria:

* Minors.
* Have a history of breast cancer or other cancers.
* Patients with vascular obstruction such as stroke.

locations.facility: Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Far Eastern Memorial Hospital
